raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Without NUMA binding, scheduler processes can drift across sockets, losing their CPU caches and touching host memory on the remote node, which adds per-step overhead and makes tail latency noisy. In a container without `SYS_NICE`, LLM serving skips binding entirely and logs `User lacks permission to set NUMA affinity, skipping NUMA node configuration for GPU`.

Only the memory-policy syscalls (`get_mempolicy` / `set_mempolicy`) are denied there; `sched_setaffinity` needs no privilege, so each rank can still be pinned to its GPU's NUMA node, and the default first-touch policy places its host memory there too. #43756 added this CPU-only fallback for the diffusion worker only; the LLM paths never opted in.

## Modifications

- `_is_numa_available()` no longer requires memory-policy permission, so a host where only CPU affinity can be set still gets bound. The `cpu_only_ok` / `require_mempolicy` opt-in is removed, so every caller gets the fallback.
- `configure_subprocess` strips the `--membind` segment before the numactl probe when memory policy is not permitted, so each rank does not log two expected rejections first.
- The `binding CPUs only` INFO line is logged where memory binding is actually skipped (the strip above, and `numa_bind_to_node`), so it also covers an explicit `--numa-node`.
- The diffusion worker call site drops the now-removed kwarg; the unit test that asserted the old skip is replaced, and the strip wiring gets a test. The diffusion CLI and env-var docs note that only CPU affinity is set without `CAP_SYS_NICE`.

Checked on 8x B300 without `SYS_NICE`: with this PR, TP0-3 are pinned to `0-85,172-257` (node 0) and TP4-7 to `86-171,258-343` (node 1); with `SGLANG_AUTO_NUMA_BIND=0` (the same no-bind path the old code took here), all ranks have affinity `0-343`. Memory placement is not enforced; `--cap-add SYS_NICE` is still needed for `--membind`.

Behavior change: with `SGLANG_CRASH_ON_NUMA_BIND_FAILURE=1`, an unprivileged pod whose allowed CPUs don't overlap the GPU's node used to start unbound (binding was skipped earlier); it now fails at launch, as the flag intends.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

`sglang serve --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --tp-size 8` on 8x B300 without `SYS_NICE`, bound (this PR) vs unbound (`SGLANG_AUTO_NUMA_BIND=0`). `python -m sglang.benchmark.serving`, random-ids, 256 in / 256 out, `--max-concurrency 64`, 1024 prompts, 256 warmup requests, `--flush-cache`. Mean ± stdev over 3 alternating rounds:

| metric | bound | unbound | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| output tok/s | 23,584 ± 222 | 22,915 ± 528 | +2.9% |
| TPOT p50 (ms) | 2.35 ± 0.02 | 2.42 ± 0.06 | -2.9% |
| TPOT p99 (ms) | 2.72 ± 0.03 | 3.03 ± 0.27 | -10% |

Bound was ahead on all three metrics in each of the three rounds, and the runs were more repeatable: run-to-run spread was 2.4x lower for throughput (±222 vs ±528 tok/s) and 9x lower for TPOT p99 (±0.03 vs ±0.27 ms).

 - PEFT `adapter_config.json` semantics are applied automatically for named adapter slots, RSLoRA, and per-layer `alpha_pattern`. Adapters that require unsupported auxiliary parameters or runtime behavior, such as DoRA, fail before weight injection instead of silently using ordinary LoRA math.
 - `--lora-merge-mode {auto|merge|dynamic}`: choose how LoRA is applied. `auto` statically merges regular weights and uses dynamic LoRA for FSDP-sharded weights to avoid full-gather peaks.
 - `--num-gpus {N}`: number of GPUs to use
-- `--numa-node {N} [N ...]`: NUMA node for each GPU worker, the i-th value for the worker on local GPU i. When unset, each worker binds its CPUs and host memory to its GPU's NUMA node on multi-socket hosts, as srt does; set `SGLANG_AUTO_NUMA_BIND=0` to turn that off. Unbound workers on a two-socket host (e.g. GB200/GB300) can drift to the other socket, which slows host-bound steps and makes latency vary run to run.
+- `--numa-node {N} [N ...]`: NUMA node for each GPU worker, the i-th value for the worker on local GPU i. When unset, each worker binds its CPUs and host memory to its GPU's NUMA node on multi-socket hosts, as srt does (CPUs only without `CAP_SYS_NICE`); set `SGLANG_AUTO_NUMA_BIND=0` to turn that off. Unbound workers on a two-socket host (e.g. GB200/GB300) can drift to the other socket, which slows host-bound steps and makes latency vary run to run.
 - `--performance-mode {manual|auto|speed|memory}` / `--mode`: preset for latency/throughput and memory defaults. `auto` is the default and dispatches residency from selected-GPU headroom and workload type: image DiTs stay resident above the 45 GiB threshold, while video DiT placement remains model-specific. It uses FSDP only for validated DiT-offload replacement paths. `speed` keeps `torch.compile` disabled unless a model-specific deployment config opts in after validation; pass `--enable-torch-compile true` to enable it explicitly. Use `manual` to keep performance-related server args under explicit user control. Explicit offload, FSDP, and parallelism flags take precedence in all modes.
 - `--direct-gpu-weight-loading {true|false}`: opt into direct GPU loading for an unquantized, GPU-resident, TP=1 DiT by materializing its complete checkpoint state dict on GPU. Compatible tensors become parameter storage without another GPU copy, while tensors requiring transforms can still need temporary allocations. It is disabled by default; startup time and peak GPU memory remain model-dependent, so benchmark the target model before deployment. It is incompatible with DiT CPU/layerwise offload and FSDP.
 - `--tp-size {N}`: tensor parallelism size. Depending on the pipeline, it can shard the DiT, one or more encoders, or both.
